description: UK cross-grain reconciliation declarations (microcosm#802, #905, #1123). Every target bound at more than one geography grain, or overlapping another target's population at a different grain, reaches a control through an exact measurement signature, a bridge or a partition, or is declared here as a subset or an unreconciled local family with its reason. tools and tests read this file through microcosm.build.uk_runtime.cross_grain_declarations; the static coverage check refuses an undeclared overlap.

bridges.reason: Each nation's official household estimate controls its census household cells (microcosm#1123, nations win): the LFS 2025 rows for the nine English regions, NRS 2025 for Scotland, Welsh Government mid-2024 rolled to 2025 for Wales, Census 2021 rolled by LPS dwelling stock for Northern Ireland. Each row covers its own legs; the census cells keep their shares within a leg.

Each English region's and nation's Table 2.2 higher rate taxpayer row for calendar 2025 controls its SPI 2023-24 area cells, which keep their shares within it (microcosm#1123). Scotland's row has no area cells: its 2023-24 cells predate the Scottish advanced rate (area_scope E, W, N).

The GB Universal Credit caseload controls the households-on-UC cells by constituency and local authority (Northern Ireland is deferred locally). Both sides count paid claims since the abf0921 re-pin (PolicyEngine/chronicle#339 splits each area-month by Stat-Xplore's Payment Indicator and the area targets bind 'Yes', microcosm#1300), so the factor sits near one, the size of DWP's 'Unknown' area, which carries no area fact, where it was the GB paid share, 0.921, applied to every area alike (microcosm#1198 review, must-fix 1). A factor more than two per cent from one means the sides no longer measure one quantity and is refused. The bound applies to each grain's GB total, the constituencies' and the authorities' sums over Great Britain, read before any group rescales them (on a surface with off-surface cells, on the pass that carries them); it does not bound each nation or English region within a grain, whose authorities the exact-signature group puts on its own constituencies.

The ONS controls use inclusive integer-age bands (0-9) and the local cells the equivalent half-open encoding (0-10), so the signatures cannot match directly; the region-tier rows (one per English region and per nation, microcosm#905) rescale both local grains over their twelve legs. The 80-89 band has no local cell.

partitions.reason: The census tenure cells divide each authority's households; shared ownership and rent-free households are not bound, so the four cells cover part of the parent and move by the authority's household reconciliation factor, keeping their shares.

DWP's constituency UC households by number of children divide each constituency's UC caseload; the published unknown-children category is not bound, so the four bands cover part of the parent and move by its reconciliation factor, keeping their published shares. The local metrics count benefit units on UC, as the parent does. Since the abf0921 re-pin the bands count paid claims, as their parent does (microcosm#1300).

Each authority's gas-connected households are its census households times its DESNZ gas meters over its electricity meters, a share of the parent; they take the census household uprating and then the authority's household reconciliation factor, keeping DESNZ's share. The households off the gas network are not bound (microcosm#1207).

fanout_sum_bridges.reason: The SPI Table 3.6 bands, summed over every band of the full compiled register (the measure-excluded £1m-and-over band included), are the UK total the Tables 3.14 and 3.15 area cells divide; the constituency and local-authority cells reconcile to it per grain. Both parts of the factor the cells take are gated, at each grain on its own. Source agreement: the bands' total over the cells' total before either side's uprating index must sit within 2% of one. Index gap: the bands grow band by band and the cells on the all-ranges index, which leaves a gap of 0.5% on this bridge; max_index_shift is that gap plus half a point, so a re-pinned index that widens it is refused.

sum_bridges.reason: The ten LFS household-composition rows partition all UK households; the nations' official estimates sum to a different total than the LFS UK figure (about 29.09m against 29.003m), and the nations win, so the national reconciliation scales the composition by one factor onto the nations' sum, keeping its shares.

household_basis_partitions.reason: The council-tax dwelling stock (MHCLG and StatsWales taxbase lines, Scotland's CTAXBASE chargeable dwellings) and each nation's official household estimate bind the same weighted household count of an area at two published levels, so the solve traded one against the other (microcosm#1284). Each English region's, Wales's and Scotland's dwelling total takes its household control and its bands move by the same factor, the area's published households per chargeable dwelling: 0.980 to 1.023 across the eleven areas on the 735820c feed. The signed assumption is that households per chargeable dwelling are the same in every band of an area. They are not exactly: multi-household dwellings concentrate in lower bands, and second homes, where still counted, in particular areas. The bands therefore bind their area's band mix and the level follows the household estimate. The tripwire refuses a factor further than 0.035 from one, the measured 0.023 with a margin. Northern Ireland has no council-tax rows. National register only: the local band cells follow the national rows by signature.

ons.rent.private_rent.reason: ONS PIPR publishes area means, not a national private-rent total the frame binds; the local-authority rows are 12 x mean x reconciled private renters (uk_private_rent_mean_to_total), so they follow the tenure cells' reconciliation. Placed renters' rents come from their BRMA's rent-officer list of rents at their region's FRS level (microcosm#1262); PIPR shares that evidence base, so the rows stay bound, but their pattern between areas is not independent validation. The rows bind PIPR's level, while the node holds each region at its FRS level, which sits below it; with the tenure rows bound, calibration closes the gap only by moving weight toward higher-rent renters within each area, a level miss declared under María's A3/A4 rulings rather than modelled.

The electricity cells are levelled onto the lcfs stage's Energy Trends level by their uprating index instead (desnz.energy_trends.gb_domestic_level; microcosm#1207, local-authority grain only).

ons.rent.private_rent_brma.reason: ONS PIPR publishes Scotland's rents as means over its 18 Broad Rental Market Areas, which overlap the councils, and no national private-rent total the frame binds. Each row is 12 x the BRMA mean x the BRMA's private renters, derived from the councils' reconciled tenure cells through Census 2022's council shares of each BRMA's renters (uk_private_rent_brma_mean_to_total), so the rows follow the tenure reconciliation and no BRMA cell is a parent or a leg of any other (microcosm#1090, #1262). Placed renters' rents come from their BRMA's rent-officer list of rents at their region's FRS level (microcosm#1262); PIPR shares that evidence base, so the rows stay bound, but their pattern between areas is not independent validation. The rows bind PIPR's level, while the node holds each region at its FRS level, which sits below it; with the tenure rows bound, calibration closes the gap only by moving weight toward higher-rent renters within each area, a level miss declared under María's A3/A4 rulings rather than modelled.
